text:
maya: Quick thought — the continuous batcher drift we saw yesterday looks like alignment between deferred coalesce and admission windows. wondering if we should intentionally align their epochs to reduce tail latency.

sam: can you paste the jitter numbers?

maya: from the repro run: 99th went from 210ms -> 470ms when deferred coalesce skewed by ~12ms vs admission window. evens out if they share epoch boundary.

priya: interesting. is this the case for long sequences or short requests too?

maya: mostly short requests (<=32 tokens). long requests dominated by model time so no clear effect.

liam: alignment might help with starved microbatches — when coalesce waits just a hair longer than admission window, we end up sending tiny partial batches into fallback path.

anja: downside: coupling increases system-wide oscillation risk. if admission policy changes, coalesce needs update too.

sam: alternative: expose a small overlap parameter instead of hard align. e.g., coalesce_start = admission_epoch_start - overlap_ms. gives us a controlled buffer.

maya: overlap param seems sensible. but need invariant: overlap_ms < min_latency_deadline to avoid repeated requeue/eviction loops.

priya: does overlap hurt fairness? a bigger overlap could let some tenants capture earlier windows consistently.

liam: true. we should make overlap tenant-aware. high-priority tenants get smaller overlap to reduce wait variance, best-effort gets larger to batch more.

maya: ops question: how do we observe misalignment? what metric turned red yesterday?

sam: we saw a spike in "partial_batch_fraction" and the new "batch_start_drift_ms" histogram. batch_start_drift_ms is the difference between admission epoch start and coalesce emission time.

anja: add a simple alert: p95(batch_start_drift_ms) > 10ms for 1m. that flagged it.

priya: proposal: (1) add overlap_ms config at scheduler-level; (2) wire tenant-priority multiplier; (3) emit drift histogram and partial_batch_fraction; (4) default overlap_ms=6ms.

liam: for safety, also add a backstop: if partial_batch_fraction > 0.25 then force immediate drain (bypass coalesce) for next N windows. avoids runaway small-batch churn.

maya: sounds good. two concerns: KV cache alignment (prefix cached tokens) and tail latency on cold starts. how does overlap affect KV cache hits?

sam: if we delay only a few ms, KV cache benefit intact. problem is if tenant requests keep jumping coalesce epochs — that'll thrash the cache because eviction heuristics operate per-epoch.

priya: maybe we should epoch-sticky KV keys: map cache footprints to logical epoch id and only evict at epoch boundaries, not per-coalesce emission. reduces thrash but adds memory headroom.

anja: memory headroom is finite. recommend making epoch-sticky cache optional per-deployment and exposing memory usage per-epoch in console.

liam: implementation note: epoch id can be Round(admission_ts / epoch_ms) so cheap to compute. small change in enqueue path to tag requests.

maya: what about rollout plan? want canary with 10% traffic on dedicated clusters first. watch p99, partial_batch_fraction, batch_start_drift_ms, kv_hit_rate.

sam: i'll draft the config flags and telemetry. can we write a small e2e test that injects deterministic jitter and asserts p99 < baseline + 50ms?

priya: yes — use the synthetic tenant harness. i'll add a jitter scenario and script to toggle overlap_ms at runtime.

anja: ops: add runbook entry: if p99 regresses, toggle overlap_ms down and trigger forced-drain backstop.

maya: LGTM. final open Q: default overlap value. priya suggested 6ms, sam?

sam: 6ms looks like the knee from local runs. with tenant multiplier we can keep safe.

maya: OK let's do: default 6ms, tenant multiplier in [0.5, 2.0], backstop threshold 0.25 partial_batch_fraction. i'll open PR for scheduler + telemetry.

deploy-bot: started CI for branch: feature/deferred-coalesce-align (build 1287) :white_check_mark:

liam: thanks — will review the PR, adding a unit that verifies epoch id tagging.

priya: i'll hook the synthetic test into the canary job.

maya: short follow-up: add a short note in the design doc about coupling risk and why overlap is opt-in per cluster. avoids surprising autoscaling interactions.

sam: noted. tagging product for console flags? @product needed to show overlap in the runtime page.

maya: pinged product. ok closing thread unless more comments. :thumbsup:
